items.title: ESP8266 Weather Station and Binary Number Challenge
items.description: An academic connected-object project built with an ESP8266. It reads environmental data from a BME280 sensor, displays the readings on an OLED and a local web server, and includes a binary number challenge: three LEDs show a value in binary. The player reads the LEDs, selects the matching decimal number with the button, checks it on the OLED, and confirms the answer.
items.technologies: ESP8266 · C++ · Arduino · BME280 · SSD1306 OLED · I²C · Wi‑Fi

items.title: Connected Weather Station with MicroPython Display and Zabbix
items.description: An academic IoT project that connects two ESP8266 boards over a local network. One Arduino/C++ board reads temperature, humidity, pressure, and estimated altitude from a BME280, controls two LEDs, and serves the readings as JSON. A second board uses MicroPython to show the data on an SSD1306 OLED, with a potentiometer for display contrast. Zabbix monitors the sensor and LED data.
items.technologies: ESP8266 · C++ · Arduino · MicroPython · BME280 · SSD1306 OLED · Zabbix · JSON · Wi‑Fi

items.title: IoT Sensor Monitoring with MQTT and Zabbix
items.description: An academic IoT system that links three microcontrollers: an ESP8266 reads BME280 measurements and exposes them as JSON while publishing readings over MQTT; a second ESP8266 displays data on an SSD1306 OLED, and an ESP32 collects GY-521 accelerometer, gyroscope, and temperature readings. Mosquitto routes messages, and Zabbix monitors the sensor endpoints.
items.technologies: ESP8266 · ESP32 · C++ · Arduino · MicroPython · BME280 · GY-521/MPU-6050 · SSD1306 OLED · MQTT · Mosquitto · Zabbix · HTTP/JSON · Wi‑Fi
